page: Amazon Web Services m7g.16xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton3 processor family. Built on the custom ARMv8 Neoverse-V1 architecture, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. It does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7g.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core performance and memory efficiency. Multi-core CPU tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the top 25% tier, reflecting the efficiency of its 64 dedicated physical cores. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with the Passmark memory score reaching the top 10% tier, supported by strong uncached read and write memory bandwidth. The instance also excels in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput, all scoring in the top 25% tier. However, single-core performance remains in the average tier across stress-ng and Geekbench tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture offers a highly competitive performance-per-watt profile, translating to qualitative cost advantages for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 instances. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale EBS volumes independently. The instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database hosting, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
